inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q Q3-2026, EPS note: 152,693k). Held flat because SBC plus award-tax withholding is expensed in the flows. Stock issued as acquisition consideration is not modelled forward because no future M&A is modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026E. Non-cash stock-based compensation 193.9 for 9M-2026 (10-Q Q3-2026 cash flow statement) annualised to ~262, plus payments related to tax withholding for stock-based compensation 174.7 for 9M-2026 taken at ~180 for the year (vesting is first-half weighted). Quanta publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 actuals: 181.9 + 112.3 = 294.2 (1.03% of revenue).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 gives a cost of equity near 9.8%; debt is ~5% of enterprise value at a ~5.5% pre-tax cost, so WACC rounds to 9.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality and AI-capex risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating lease cost is already inside adjusted EBITDA, so operating lease liabilities (520.8 at Q3 2026) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases (48.8) are inside total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). Non-controlling interests are deducted once, in the equity bridge, at ~12x annualised NCI income (31.1 for 9M-2026); book NCI is 86.2.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company, specialty contractor). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 is FY2026E, not FY2025: nine months are reported, the year is guided (revenue 41.3-41.6bn, FCF 2.5-3.0bn) and the balance sheet anchor is 30 Sep 2026, so starting the build at FY2025 would count nine months of FY2026 cash twice (once in the flows, once in net debt). Year 1 is FY2027. Q4-2026 cash flow (~0.3-0.8bn, roughly $2-5/share) is left out of both the flows and net debt, which is slightly conservative. reported_fcf and last_fcf are the FY2026 guidance midpoint, not an actual; FY2025 actual reported FCF was 1,620.8 and owner FCF 1,326.6. Interest income is not stripped because the company carries net debt. Growth paths are organic only from the FY2026E base: no further acquisitions are modelled and no acquisition cash is deducted, i.e. future M&A is assumed value-neutral. Acquired-intangible amortisation therefore runs off in da_pct_path (it is non-cash but tax-deductible). Buybacks: none in 9M-2026, 134.6 in FY2025; the flat share count is a modelling convention that Quanta funds mainly through net-share settlement (the award-tax line), not open-market repurchases. Working-capital capture is negative: a contractor's receivables and contract assets grow with revenue. 2026 was the opposite (contract liabilities rose from 3.26bn to 5.54bn and DSO fell from 66 to 50 days), which is why FY2026 guided FCF sits above the component-built year-1 figure; that prepayment inflow is not carried forward.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at ~12x annualised NCI income
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q Q3-2026: net income attributable to NCI 31.1 for nine months; book NCI 86.2

historical_growth.notes: FY2020/FY2022 to FY2025 annual figures. FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less award-tax withholding; no interest strip, net debt): FY2020 738.9, FY2022 514.5, FY2025 1,326.6. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are close, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Equity growth is flattered by stock issued for acquisitions, and all of the revenue CAGRs include acquired revenue; the forward paths are organic and are set from backlog and guidance, not from these CAGRs. FY2026 guided revenue growth is ~45.5%.

base.rationale: Growth: 12-month backlog was 38.4bn at Q3 2026 against 22.3bn a year earlier (+72%), which supports ~20% in FY2027 before decelerating to GDP-plus. Margin: FY2026E adjusted EBITDA margin is ~11% (10.9% for nine months, 12.1% in Q3) against 10.1% in FY2025; held at 11% and faded to 10.5% as the data-center mix normalises. D&A: depreciation ~1.3% plus acquired-intangible amortisation running off from ~1.4% to ~0.2%. Capex 2.2% gross (2.4% in 9M-2026, 2.1% in FY2025) easing as growth slows. Cash tax 25% (FY2025 effective 25.0%, cash paid 347 against a 348 provision). Cap multiple 15x for a cyclical contractor; it binds against a 17.2x Gordon value.

scenario_narratives.base: The grid and large-load build-out continues but stops accelerating. The 63.7bn backlog converts on schedule, giving ~20% organic growth in FY2027 and low-double-digit growth in FY2028, after which utility capex and data-center interconnection grow at a high-single-digit rate that fades to 3%. Craft-labour scarcity caps conversion speed but also protects pricing, so adjusted EBITDA margin holds near the FY2026 level of 11% before easing to 10.5% as the data-center and EPC mix normalises. Tuck-in M&A continues but is treated as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: A multi-year electrification supercycle: hyperscaler and advanced-manufacturing load, transmission expansion and gas/renewable interconnection all run together, backlog keeps growing faster than revenue, and Quanta's scale in linemen and its in-house transformer and civil capabilities let it take share from regional contractors. Organic growth stays in the teens through FY2029 and margins step up to 12% on turnkey data-center and EPC work, with customer prepayments keeping working-capital needs light.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex is cut and the fastest-growing part of backlog (large-load and generation EPC, mostly cancellable or deferrable) is pushed out. Revenue stalls in FY2028 and falls in FY2029-30, leaving the utility MSA base. Fixed-price exposure on large projects and under-absorbed labour take adjusted EBITDA margin back to ~9%, the pre-2025 level, and the debt taken on for 2024-26 acquisitions (goodwill and intangibles bought at peak multiples) earns less than planned. A wildfire or casualty liability event sits on top of this path and is not separately provisioned.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: a large share of incremental backlog is tied to one demand source (AI data-center power), contractor earnings are cyclical, and FY2026 margins are at a record. Base held at 50%: it already assumes the record backlog converts and record margins largely persist. Bull trimmed to 30%: it needs sustained teens growth, a further margin step-up and continued customer prepayments at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Quanta is valued as a cyclical specialty contractor at a record point in its cycle. Owner FCF charges SBC and the cash tax withheld on vesting awards (together ~1.1% of revenue), deducts maintenance and growth capex, and treats growth as a consumer of working capital. The model gives full credit for the backlog in FY2027-28 but does not capitalise FY2026's working-capital inflow or assume the terminal buyer pays more than 15x owner FCF. On that basis the current price implies an outcome at or beyond the bull scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: the 15x cap binds in the base case; each 1x is worth roughly $13/share
Margin durability: each 1pp of adjusted EBITDA margin held across the whole horizon is worth roughly $45-50/share in the base case (about $27 of it in the terminal value)
M&A is assumed value-neutral; if tuck-ins keep earning above the cost of capital the model understates value, and if 2024-26 deals were bought at peak multiples it overstates it
Working capital: contract liabilities of 5.5bn are customer prepayments that would unwind if large-load project starts slow
FY0 is a guided year, not a reported one; Q4-2026 results replace the base revenue and SBC anchors
